cards.back: Tokenises text, builds an inverted index and scores shared words weighted by rarity. Fast, explainable and best when the user types the exact thing they want.
Synonyms and paraphrases: it only matches words that actually appear in the document.
Embeds the query and finds the nearest chunk vectors in a vector database. It shines when the user's words differ from the document's, like "baby leave" vs "parental leave policy".
Exact tokens, numbers and negation, such as an ID like HR-4512.
Run keyword and dense searches in parallel, take the top 50 or so from each, fuse the lists, then send the fused list to a reranker.
The robust default way to fuse ranked lists, using the usual constant k = 60. A weighted sum of normalised scores also works but needs tuning.
Model-expanded keywords: keyword speed with some synonym handling, but it needs its own model and index.
Matches exact field values such as permissions, dates, regions and types. It is not a relevance ranking.
Apply the metadata filter inside every search, never after it.
Use a small model to make follow-ups standalone, pull out filters, expand acronyms from a glossary and sometimes search two or three alternative phrasings in parallel.

quiz.q: A user searches for the exact ID HR-4512. Which search type finds it most reliably?
quiz.why: Keyword search matches the exact token, while dense search is weak at exact tokens and numbers.

quiz.q: Which query is dense search best placed to handle?
choices: "baby leave" finding the parental leave policy
A query that hinges on the word "not"
Only documents from the India region
quiz.why: Dense search matches meaning, so it works when the user's words differ from the document's.

quiz.q: What is the safe default for enterprise documents full of IDs, names and jargon?
quiz.why: Hybrid covers each method's blind spot, and reranking sorts the fused list.

quiz.q: How should keyword and dense searches run in a hybrid setup?
choices: Keyword first, then dense on its results
Dense first, then keyword on its results
Only one, picked at random per query
quiz.why: The two searches are independent, so they run in parallel and their lists are fused.

quiz.q: Where should a permission filter be applied?
quiz.why: Filtering inside the search means ranking only ever considers permitted chunks.

quiz.q: A user asks "what about contractors?" as a follow-up. What fixes this best?
choices: Rewrite it into a standalone question
quiz.why: Query rewriting turns follow-ups into standalone questions, which often helps more than changing the index.
